hints: Notice where P sits on the $s$-distance graph at $t = 0$: it has positive $s$ and lies on the falling slope just to the right of a crest.
Connect the rightward direction of travel to what P feels next: the whole shape shifts right, so the higher crest to the left of P arrives at P.
Direct the comparison: the $s$-$t$ graph at $t = 0$ must therefore start positive and first increase to a peak before decreasing through zero.
walkthrough: Look at the given $s$ against distance graph at $t = 0$: point P has $s > 0$ and is on the downhill side after the peak.
Recall the rule for a travelling profile: with direction of travel to the right, the displacement at fixed P is replaced by the displacement that was just to its left.
Just to the left of P the wave is higher, near the crest, so in the next small time $s$ at P must increase.
After that crest passes, P must then fall through zero to a trough and oscillate with the same sinusoidal shape and period $T$.
Only a $s$-$t$ graph that starts positive, rises briefly to a maximum, then falls fits this cause-and-effect chain. This is option D.

options.A: This starts at positive $s$ but falls immediately, which would mean the crest to the left of P is moving away from P.
options.B: This starts at $s = 0$ and rises, which describes the origin point at $t = 0$, not point P which already has positive $s$.
options.C: This starts near $s = 0$ and first moves negative, which is opposite to P being pulled up toward the approaching crest.
options.D: This starts at positive $s$, rises a little to a maximum then falls through zero, matching P being just to the right of the crest as the wave moves right.
